purpose: R250 non-financial HS300 revenue-growth stability factor versus a matched quality-cash control

universe.industry_source: current ext_hy_ths industry snapshot; not historical PIT

factor.formula: revenue_growth_stability_4q_low = -std(g_t, g_t_minus_1, g_t_minus_2, g_t_minus_3), where g_t = single_quarter_revenue_t / single_quarter_revenue_t_minus_4 - 1; higher means more stable year-over-year single-quarter revenue growth
factor.pit_rule: single-quarter revenue from cumulative YTD reports; effective date = statutory reporting deadline + 3 calendar days; values expire after 500 calendar days

pit_audit.rule: single-quarter revenue from cumulative YTD reports; effective date = statutory reporting deadline + 3 calendar days; latest report expires after 500 calendar days

samples.rolling_1y: 252-trading-day rolling compounded return over the stitched 2023-2026 curve
samples.recent_12m: last 252 trading-day returns of the stitched 2023-2026 curve

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four components proportionally
execution.stitching: two segment returns compounded into one curve; first day of each later segment skipped

caveats: Only four year-over-year single-quarter growth observations are used, so stability estimates can be noisy.
The standard deviation is sensitive to one-off revenue shocks and low prior-year bases.
The discovery segment has only about 19 months because two years of quarterly history are required.
Financial values are current snapshots and may contain restatements.
The industry snapshot used to exclude financials is current rather than historical PIT.
The full curve is stitched from two system-engine segments; segment boundaries can reset an open position.
Trade P&L shares are contribution diagnostics from two segments each starting at 1,000,000 notional, not a compounded-return decomposition.
The factor is research-only until every preregistered gate passes; passing would justify paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
